name: Heap Sort
description: Uses a max-heap data structure to sort. First builds a max-heap from the array, then repeatedly extracts the maximum element and places it at the end.
aim: Sort by building a max-heap from the input array (O(n)), then repeatedly swapping the root (maximum) with the last unsorted element and heapifying down (n × O(log n)).
howItWorks: Build a max-heap from the array using bottom-up heapification
Swap root (maximum) with last element — last element is now sorted
Heapify down the new root to restore max-heap property
Repeat from step 2 until heap size is 1
Array is sorted in ascending order

time.bestCase: Building heap is O(n), n extractions each O(log n)
time.averageCase: Consistent performance across all input types
time.worstCase: No worst-case degradation unlike Quick Sort

complexity.spaceDescription: In-place using the input array as heap storage

realWorld: Systems requiring guaranteed O(n log n) with O(1) space
Priority queue operations requiring sorted output
Sorting in embedded systems with limited memory
whenToUse: Guaranteed O(n log n) with no extra space required
When worst-case matters and memory is tight
Heap sort is preferred over Quick Sort when worst case must be avoided
alternatives: Quick Sort — faster in practice due to cache effects
Merge Sort — stable with same complexity but O(n) space
Intro Sort — hybrid that combines Quick + Heap + Insertion (used in C++ STL)
